recognitionRules: Use Didot for the main proposition and Optima for the explanatory route.
Keep Reader map and Evidence links in consistent footer positions.
Use plum and teal as restrained editorial accents on warm paper.

quote: Read the argument. Follow the record. Decide what needs another look.
rightsSummary: Original fictional identity and vector logos; portable font binaries retain their licenses. Source family dependencies and substitutions are documented.
logoDirection: Use ATLAS READING ROOM in a high-contrast Didot wordmark with a small Optima edition line. No globe or map pin.
invariants: Use Didot for the main proposition and Optima for the explanatory route.
Keep Reader map and Evidence links in consistent footer positions.
Use plum and teal as restrained editorial accents on warm paper.
adaptations: A short briefing can retain the reader map and one linked evidence page.
Print editions replace links with page references.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
decisionStatus: Template-derived editorial identity for the requested library. Creative rules are proposed production directions; no real organization or official endorsement is asserted.
